checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Three scenes in order, ~3s each: Earth, Jupiter, Saturn
must.why: Only Earth and Jupiter clips are available. No Saturn scene was supplied, so it cannot be confirmed and is probably missing.

must.item: Each scene shows its caption exactly, with 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible throughout
must.why: Scene 1 reads 'Launchad'. Scene 2 duplicates 'Voyager 1' and has a spacing glitch in 'flyby:1979'. In both scenes the labels fade out before the scene ends.

must.item: Probe consistently has a large dish and booms
must.why: The dish and booms are present, but the probe's design and booms differ noticeably between the Earth and Jupiter scenes.

must.item: Jupiter is banded and Saturn has prominent rings, with no Uranus or Neptune
must.why: Jupiter is clearly banded with the Great Red Spot. No Saturn scene was shown.

must.item: No Uranus or Neptune claims and no conflicting dates
must.why: None of the visible text or imagery mentions Uranus or Neptune, and the dates shown are consistent.
Audio cannot be judged from still frames. The assistant claims the clip is silent.

exact_text.read_as: Jupiter flyby:1979 (missing space, italic, overlapping glyphs)
not visible in the supplied frames

faults.what: Scene 2 shows 'Voyager 1' twice, and 'Jupiter flyby:1979' has a spacing glitch.
Labels fade out before the end of each scene, so they are not visible throughout.
The probe's design changes between the Earth and Jupiter scenes.
No Saturn scene appears in the supplied output, and the clip is split into separate files.

summary: The Earth and Jupiter scenes look good, but 'Launchad' is misspelled, the Jupiter labels are duplicated and glitchy, labels fade out early, the probe design changes between scenes, and no Saturn scene was supplied.
